title: Resilience & Fallback Sales Deck for Critical Inference
author: Nadia Kline
body:
Overview
========

Purpose: A field-ready deck and evidence pack for Redwood Inference's resilience and graceful-degradation story, aimed at mission-critical inference (fraud detection, live support routing, automated decisioning). It covers positioning, differentiators, a slide-by-slide outline, pilot pricing guidance, a case study, rollout patterns and a security FAQ.

Use: Sales engineers and account teams proposing pilots to prospects who need high availability, predictable latency and clear fallback guarantees.

Key message (one-liner)
-----------------------
"Predictable inference when everything else fails: keep latency SLOs, control unit economics, and preserve confidentiality with tiered fallbacks and multi-path routing."

Positioning & Messaging
-----------------------
- For platform and infra teams that cannot afford interruptions, Redwood offers a runtime and control plane built around reliability and graceful degradation rather than best-case throughput.
- Compared with single-endpoint cloud APIs or home-grown runtimes, Redwood pairs an operational playbook (canaries, automatic fallback policies, cross-region routing) with cost controls, so resilience is both measurable and affordable.
- Lead with instrumentable SLAs (uptime, latency SLOs, error budgets) and automated fallbacks that keep failures away from the application.

Competitive Brief
-----------------
Compared against: public cloud model endpoints, API-first LLM providers, self-managed inference stacks.

Differentiators
- Smart routing and fallbacks to cheaper/compatible variants or regionally isolated Dedicated pools when primary capacity is tight.
- Observability: token-level cost and latency, route tracing, regression alerts tied to prompt sets.
- Operational guarantees: canaries, A/B rollouts, rollback triggers on quality and latency thresholds.
- Cost controls: workload-specific batching and caching, quantization profiles, per-route unit economics.

Performance & SLO snapshots
- Hosted API: p50 35–60ms, p95 110–220ms depending on model size and sequence length.
- Dedicated reserved pools: p50 20–40ms, p95 70–150ms for optimized-medium models.
- Platform SLA examples: 99.95% uptime, route-level p95 targets with error budgets tied to token-level retries.

Pitch Deck Outline (12 slides)
------------------------------
1) Cover: logo, prospect, date, pilot ask.
2) Problem: latency spikes, serving outages, cost overruns, regulatory constraints.
3) Why it matters: KPI impact (abandon rate, fraud loss, revenue per minute).
4) Value prop: unified runtime + fallbacks + observability.
5) How it works: routing -> KV/prefix cache -> model variants -> fallback paths.
6) Resilience model: SLOs, retry/circuit-breaker, fallback tiers (same-model-smaller, distilled variant, cached response).
7) Security & compliance: VPC/private, KMS/HSM, audit logs.
8) Pricing & pilot structure.
9) Case study.
10) Pilot plan & success criteria.
11) Next steps & commercial ask.
12) Appendix & technical contacts.

Pilot Pricing Guidance
----------------------
Principle: price resilience pilots for predictability, not just tokens.

Sample pilot models (example guidance):
- Trial (proof-of-concept): 2–4 weeks, $0 setup, free credits up to $2.5k for hosted API with monitoring instrumentation.
- Resilience Pilot (recommended): 6–8 weeks on a small dedicated pool (N GPU equivalents), $15k/month (discounted trial price), including SRE onboarding, route dashboards and fallback policy setup.
- Proof to Commit: e.g., 2x pilot throughput committed for 12 months at $45k/month with priority support and a 99.95% SLA.

Per-token framing (token-equivalent units, TEUs):
- Hosted baseline: $0.0007 per generation token for medium models (ballpark).
- Dedicated amortized: roughly $0.0003–$0.0005 per token with reserved throughput and batching on steady workloads.

Commercial ask script
- "We suggest a six-week Resilience Pilot: a small Dedicated pool, three critical routes instrumented, two fallback tiers. If you hit the success criteria (p95 under X ms, <0.5% fallbacks to cached responses), we turn the telemetry into a reserved-capacity proposal."

Objections & Responses
----------------------
- "We cannot tolerate any data leakage to third parties." -> Private deployment in a customer-managed VPC or on-prem; keys stay in your KMS/HSM; audit logs flow to your SIEM.
- "What if primary capacity runs out?" -> Multi-tier fallbacks: 1) your Dedicated pool, 2) a lightweight compatible hosted model, 3) cached/templated responses with graceful messaging. Every fallback is metered and visible on the dashboard.
- "How do you guarantee fallback quality?" -> Fallback models are pre-evaluated on your prompt set with automatic quality gates (BLEU/accuracy threshold or your eval harness).

Technical Appendix: Integration & Rollout
-----------------------------------------
Pilot prerequisites:
- Test prompt corpus (1k–10k examples) with edge cases and realistic lengths.
- Success metrics: p95 target, fallback rate ceiling, quality thresholds.
- Network: allowlist Redwood control-plane IPs for Dedicated/VPC, or peering details for Private.

Canary / Rollout recipe
1) Provision the route in staging with tracing.
2) Run synthetic traffic for 48–72 hours; collect p50/p95/p99 and errors.
3) Canary 2–5% of production traffic with automatic rollback if daily error rate exceeds 0.5% or p95 increases by >40%.
4) Step up to 25%, watch for 72 hours, then cut over.

Sample API snippet (fallback policy)
```json
{ "route": "/messages/generate", "slo": { "p95_ms": 150 }, "fallback_policy": [
  { "type": "same-model-quantized", "max_latency_ms": 200 },
  { "type": "smaller-variant", "model": "redwood-compact-3b", "max_latency_ms": 300 },
  { "type": "kv_cache_response", "max_age_seconds": 3600 }
] }
```

Case Study: ParcelPro (logistics)
---------------------------------
Context: ParcelPro runs real-time address normalization and delivery exception triage and saw serving outages during peak events.

Challenge: peak demand pushed p95 above 700ms and caused ~4% request failures, delaying deliveries and flooding support.

Solution: Dedicated pool for critical routes, multi-tier fallback (quantized variant + cached responses), prefix-KV caching for repetitive normalizations.

Outcome (pilot):
- p95 from 700ms to 120ms on the critical route.
- Application-visible failures from 4% to 0.03%.
- Peak-window unit cost down 31% through batching and quantization.

Security & Compliance FAQ
-------------------------
Q: Where is data stored and how long is it kept?
A: Residency is per customer. Hosted offers region controls and per-route retention (default 60 days for logs, 30 days for KV cache metadata). Private deployments follow customer policy.

Q: Bring your own KMS/HSM?
A: Yes: AWS KMS, GCP KMS and customer HSMs for key wrapping and artifact signing.

Q: Audit logs and SIEM?
A: Request/response metadata, authorization events and fallback activations export to S3/BigQuery/your SIEM.

Q: Certifications?
A: SOC 2 Type II and annual third-party penetration testing; artifacts under NDA.

Q: How are fallbacks tested for safety and leakage?
A: Same onboarding eval harness as primary models, plus tokenizer-based leakage scans and prompt-perturbation tests.
